questions.question: What happens in a Rails request-response cycle?
questions.title: The Rails Request-Response Cycle
questions.direct_answer: When a request hits Rails: 1) the router (config/routes.rb) matches the URL + verb to a controller#action; 2) the controller action runs, with params available (params[:id]); 3) the action talks to models (find, where, create) and other services; 4) the action renders a response (render json:, render :index, redirect_to) or a view; 5) Rails sends the response (HTML or JSON) back to the browser. Middleware sits before the router (parsing, sessions, cookies). The cycle is: browser -> middleware -> router -> controller -> models -> render -> browser. Every Rails request follows this; understanding it is how you debug where a bug lives.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you can describe the cycle (router -> controller -> models -> render) and know where each part lives (routes.rb, the controller, models).
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Not knowing which layer owns a bug (routing? controller? model?), or skipping the router in your mental model.
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Browser -> middleware -> router (routes.rb) -> controller (action + params) -> models -> render -> browser. Every request follows this; it tells you where a bug lives.

sections.title: Browser to Router to Controller to Model and Back
sections.content: When a request hits Rails: one, the router (config slash routes.rb) matches the URL and verb to a controller hash action; two, the controller action runs, with params available (params id); three, the action talks to models (find, where, create) and other services; four, the action renders a response (render json, render index, redirect_to) or a view; five, Rails sends the response (HTML or JSON) back to the browser. Middleware sits before the router for parsing, sessions, and cookies. The cycle is browser to middleware to router to controller to models to render to browser. Every Rails request follows this; understanding it is how you debug where a bug lives.

sections.title: The Request Cycle
sections.content:
browser -> middleware -> router -> controller -> models -> render -> browser.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  B[browser] --> Mi[middleware]
  Mi --> R[router: routes.rb]
  R --> C[controller action + params]
  C --> M[models: find/where/create]
  M --> Re[render / redirect]
  Re --> B
```

sections.title: The request cycle
sections.content:
```ruby
# Browser sends: GET /posts/42
#
# 1) Middleware (parsing, sessions, cookies) runs first.
#
# 2) Router matches the URL + verb:
#    config/routes.rb
#      get '/posts/:id', to: 'posts#show'
#
# 3) Controller action runs (params available):
class PostsController < ApplicationController
  def show
    @post = Post.find(params[:id])   # 4) model: find the row
    # 5) render a response:
    render :show                      # app/views/posts/show.html.erb
    #   or for an API: render json: @post
  end
end
#
# 6) Rails sends the response (HTML or JSON) to the browser.
#
# Debugging: where does the bug live? routing? controller? model? the view?
```

sections.title: Common Mistakes
items: Not knowing which layer owns a bug — routing, controller, or model.
Skipping the router in your mental model (it's where 404s and wrong-action bugs live).
Forgetting middleware (sessions, params parsing) runs before the router.

sections.title: Key Takeaways
items: Cycle: browser -> middleware -> router -> controller -> models -> render -> browser.
The router (routes.rb) matches URL + verb to controller#action; params become available.
The controller action talks to models (find, where, create) and renders a response.
Render is render json: (API), render :index (view), or redirect_to.
Knowing the cycle tells you which layer a bug lives in (routing? controller? model?).
